title: Developer Experience Docs Playbook: SDK guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, Site Ops, and Canonical Fixes
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose:
This playbook defines standards and operational procedures for developer experience (DevEx) documentation at Redwood Inference focused on: SDK guides, quickstarts & templates, API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and the canonical fixes for top support issues. The goal is to ensure high-quality, discoverable, and maintainable docs that reduce time-to-value for customers and reduce support load for the DevEx and Support teams.

Scope:
- All SDK guides (Python, JavaScript, Go, Java) shipped in the public docs/SDK repos.
- All quickstarts and templates used for onboarding new users and sales demos.
- API examples embedded in the docs site and SDK repos.
- Docs-site operating procedures (publishing, QA, CI).
- Top support issues and canonical fixes (living list).

Ownership and Roles
- Docs owner: Developer Experience team (primary contact: Aisha Patel).
- Code owner: SDK engineering leads (per-repo OWNERS file).
- Reviewer pool: Marcus Liu (Platform), Sofia Martinez (Support).
- Escalation: See section "On-call & Escalation".

Standards and Structure (required)
1) Page anatomy (applies to all SDK guides & quickstarts)
   - Title (short, descriptive)
   - Short intro (1-2 paragraphs that summarize intent and prerequisites)
   - TL;DR code snippet (copy-paste runnable example)
   - Step-by-step quickstart (numbered)
   - Reference section (API params, config table)
   - Troubleshooting / FAQ (common errors and fixes)
   - Related links (other pages, SDK repo, issue tracker)

2) Template frontmatter (YAML in docs repository) - required fields:
   | field | description | example |
   |---|---:|---|
   | title | page title | "Python quickstart: text generation" |
   | summary | 1-line summary | "Create your first Redwood text generation call" |
   | sdk | SDK(s) covered | "python, js" |
   | tags | search tags | "quickstart, getting-started" |

3) Code snippets and examples
   - Provide minimal, runnable examples for Python and JavaScript in every SDK guide.
   - Include a streaming example where applicable.
   - Sanitize API keys in examples and refer to env var usage: REDWOOD_API_KEY.

Example: Python quickstart (TL;DR snippet)
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ["REDWOOD_API_KEY"])
res = client.generate("Write a 50-word product blurb for Redwood Inference")
print(res.text)
(Explain required package and install command: pip install redwood-inference>=0.8.0)

Docs-site operating procedures (publishing and QA)
- Branching model: docs live in docs-site repo on `main` with PR-based changes.
- Required review: docs PRs must include at least one DevEx reviewer + one SDK owner for code samples.
- CI checks (automated):
  1) link-checker (broken-link rate must be < 1%)
  2) lint (markdownlint rules)
  3) code-snippet test runner (runs Python/JS snippets in isolated env)
  4) accessibility check (axe-core).
- Publishing cadence: canary deploy to docs-staging after merge; promote to production once staging smoke tests pass or after 24 hours.

Publishing runbook (high level)
1) Update content on feature branch.
2) Add/modify tests (snippet-runner unit).
3) Create PR and add reviewers.
4) CI must pass: link-checker, snippet-runner, linter.
5) Merge to main. Docs-staging builds automatically.
6) QA: DevExp owner signs off in staging (check examples run and assets load).
7) Promote to production via deployment job in the CI pipeline.

SLOs & Metrics for docs site (measure quarterly)
- Publish-to-production time (median aim < 6 hours after PR merge)
- Broken-link rate (target < 0.5%)
- Snippet failure rate (target < 0.1%)
- Average time to triage doc-related support ticket (target < 48 hours)

SDK Guides and Quickstarts (content rules)
- Each SDK guide should have: installation, auth, example request, error handling, and pagination/streaming section if applicable.
- Quickstarts must finish in under 10 minutes and include minimal prerequisites.
- Templates: provide repo-level quickstart templates under `/templates/quickstarts/<sdk>/<use-case>/` (e.g., /templates/quickstarts/python/generation).

API Examples & Best Practices
- Use realistic payloads but keep them small. Avoid PII in examples.
- Demonstrate error handling for rate limit (HTTP 429) and retry logic (exponential backoff).
- Show both blocking and streaming consumption patterns.

Example: JS exponential backoff pseudo-code
async function callWithRetry(fn) {
  let attempt = 0;
  while (attempt < 5) {
    try {
      return await fn();
    } catch (err) {
      if (err.status === 429) {
        await sleep(2 ** attempt * 250);
        attempt += 1;
        continue;
      }
      throw err;
    }
  }
  throw new Error('max retries reached');
}

Top support issues and canonical fixes (living list)
- This section is a prioritized list of recurring problems surfaced by Support/DevEx with tested fixes that should be copy-pastable into docs. Update monthly.

1) Symptom: Snippets fail with "auth error: missing API key"
   - Root cause: Example uses placeholder key or env var not documented.
   - Fix: Add setup step and ensure examples call `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...` in README. Update snippet-runner to validate presence of env var.

2) Symptom: Streaming examples hang on first token
   - Root cause: Missing `flush()`/event loop drain in sample client or underlying HTTP client not configured for chunked transfer.
   - Fix: Provide a streaming snippet using SDK's streaming helper and call out required client version (>=0.8.2).

3) Symptom: Docs link to deprecated API params (e.g., `temperature_scale`)
   - Root cause: Out-of-date examples after API revision.
   - Fix: Run `scripts/check-deprecated-params.py` during PR and update docs to use canonical `temperature`. Add CI failure if deprecated param found.

4) Symptom: Quickstart fails in corporate network due to blocked telemetry uploads
   - Root cause: SDK tries to call home during first-run telemetry.
   - Fix: Document env var to disable telemetry: REDWOOD_TELEMETRY=0 and update quickstart to include offline option.

5) Symptom: Users hit rate limits quickly in demo scripts
   - Root cause: demo uses naive concurrency.
   - Fix: Add concurrency limiter example and recommend SDK batching helper with configuration sample.

6) Symptom: Broken links to SDK repo examples after repo restructure
   - Root cause: hard-coded links in docs.
   - Fix: Migrate links to use canonical redirects and update link-checker to validate 301/302 as warning only.

Canonical Fix Template (copy into doc PRs)
- TL;DR: one-line summary of fix.
- Repro steps: numbered steps to reproduce.
- Root cause: short explanation.
- Fix applied: code/config diff or CLI commands.
- Tests added: list of automated checks added to CI.

Example canonical fix entry (for auth error)
- TL;DR: Ensure REDWOOD_API_KEY is set in quickstart environment and the snippet-runner validates presence.
- Repro steps: 1) Clone quickstart 2) Run example without setting env var 3) Observe 401.
- Root cause: missing explicit setup step.
- Fix applied: Added preamble to quickstart README and snippet-runner env validation.
- Tests added: snippet-runner now fails fast if REDWOOD_API_KEY missing.

Templates and Checklists (for authors)
- PR checklist: [ ] Title and summary present, [ ] TL;DR snippet verified, [ ] CI passes (lint, link-checker, snippet-runner), [ ] Reviewer assigned, [ ] Related pages updated.
- Release checklist for docs: [ ] Changelog entry, [ ] Smoke tests in staging passed, [ ] Update SDK changelog if code sample changed.

On-call & Escalation
- If a production docs outage (site down or severe broken links > 5% of pages) occurs, notify #eng-docs and #eng-sre. PagerDuty escalation: DevEx-SRE rota.
- For recurring content issues where Support tickets exceed 10 in a week: open a triage issue in the DevEx backlog and schedule a 1-hour Triage + Fix session.

Maintenance cadence
- Quarterly audit: check all quickstarts, top 20 API examples, and top 25 search terms.
- Monthly: update "Top support issues" with recent tickets and fixes.

References and tools
- Docs repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs-site (internal)
- Snippet runner: https://github.com/redwood-inference/snippet-runner (internal)
- Link-checker config: /.github/link-checker-config.yaml
- CI job names: docs-lint, docs-link-check, docs-snippet-runner, docs-staging-deploy

Appendix: Example table for quickstart requirements
| Requirement | Minimum version | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Python | 3.9 | Test in 3.9/3.10/3.11 on CI |
| redwood-inference SDK | 0.8.0 | Include changelog link |
| Node | 16 | LTS recommended |
